findings.quote: **Mental rotation** asks whether two views can represent the same rigid object after rotation. A true rotation preserves distances, adjacency, handedness/chirality, and the relative arrangement of parts. A mirror image is not generally obtainable by rotation alone.
findings.problem: The recorded goal includes rotation-comparison work, but the lesson never develops a concrete paired-view comparison; it only states general invariants and the reflection distinction.

illustrations.position_quote: **Mental rotation** asks whether two views can represent the same rigid object after rotation.
illustrations.description: Show two labeled 3D objects from different viewpoints, with one true rotation match and one mirror-image nonmatch, preserving visible adjacency and handedness cues.
illustrations.why: A side-by-side comparison would make the central rotation-versus-reflection test concrete instead of leaving it as abstract prose.

illustrations.position_quote: Tracking the folds causes two squares to map to the same cube-face orientation before all six distinct faces are filled. The pattern is therefore **not a valid cube net**.
